1. "Six files under `.claude/rules/` plus `CODEOWNERS` — all **Tier 1 Governance**. Two `.claude/skills/` files, which are **not** Tier 1 (no `frozenFiles.md` entry, no CODEOWNERS rule). Four `.docs/` files."

2. "**`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are untouched. No CI workflow changed** — `.github/workflows/` is byte-identical; the only `.github/` file touched is `copilot-instructions.md`, a derived artifact that gates nothing." — verify with `git diff --name-only ec9d161 7b9b5dc -- AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md .github/`.
3. `CODEOWNERS` new block. Verify the exact text at HEAD:
```
# ── TIER 3: Component style files (co-located *.css.ts) ────────
# Placed last among the components/ rules — CODEOWNERS uses last-match-wins, not
# most-specific-wins — so this overrides the heavier Tier 2 directory rules above
# (header/footer/product-tile/etc.) for style files specifically.
overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts   @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b
```
   - Is this byte-for-byte accurate (flag paraphrase)?
   - Is it actually placed LAST in the file? Or just last among the components/ rules? Report what actually follows it in CODEOWNERS. The doc says "placed **last in the file** on purpose" in one place and the comment says "last among the components/ rules" — check which is true.
   - Verify the claim "`CODEOWNERS:186` strips the Tier 1/2 approver from every `.css.ts` under `overrides/app/components/`" — is the rule on line 186? Report the real line number of the rule line.
   - Also check: is there any LATER rule in CODEOWNERS that would re-match `.css.ts` files and override this one? If so the claim is wrong.
4. "**Was:** 'theme changes go through the UI designer' was unconditional. **Now:** it depends on the file path." — verify against `git show ec9d161:AGENTS.md` and ec9d161 rules files, and HEAD.
5. "Three rules files were edited to document this — `frozenFiles.md:44`, `protectedFiles.md:58`, and a new ~50-line section at `overrideStyling.md:170`." — verify each line number at HEAD contains what's described, and that the overrideStyling.md section starting at :170 is really ~50 lines.
6. Quote from `overrideStyling.md:191`:
> removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic* backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an optional nice-to-have
   Verify byte-for-byte and the line number.
7. "`overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` was added to the Tier 2 Global Shell list and to CODEOWNERS, with the rationale at `protectedFiles.md:23`: *"the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission."*" — verify the line number, quote, and that it IS in the Global Shell section (not another section). Also verify the CODEOWNERS entry — the doc later cites `CODEOWNERS:93`; verify that line number.
8. "**`components.md:72`** — a new exception letting Context-backed, app-wide static-copy hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) be called from presentational leaves ... It's explicitly narrow: *"content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page."*" — verify line 72 and the quote byte-for-byte.
9. "**`testing.md:5`** — a component gets its own test file even when its behaviour is covered transitively. Resolve the duplication by scoping what that file asserts, not by omitting it." — verify line 5 of `.claude/rules/testing.md` at HEAD says that.
10. "**`code-quality` and `new-component` skills** — hardened to match: a `play` function elsewhere **no longer substitutes** for a component's own test file. `/code-quality` will now flag MISSING TEST on files that passed before." — verify the actual skill file diffs in the range.
11. "`542ac65`'s message states: *"Edited under verified tier-1-approvers identity (gh api user + team membership check) per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval process."*" — verify with `git log -1 --format=%B 542ac65` byte-for-byte.
12. "Of the other commits touching Tier 1 files, none carries an equivalent statement — including `7b9b5dc`, which modifies `.storybook/main.js` (Tier 1, `frozenFiles.md:112`)." — verify: (a) which commits in the range touch Tier 1 files (check every changed path against frozenFiles.md's lists — including `package.json` root, `.storybook/`, `.claude/rules/`, `CODEOWNERS`, `scripts/hooks/`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/`, `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`, `overrides/app/theme/index.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `vitest.config.*`); (b) whether any of those commit messages carries a tier-1 statement; (c) whether `.storybook/main.js` is Tier 1 at `frozenFiles.md:112` specifically — report the real line number.
   IMPORTANT: `98bd633` modifies `package-lock.json` and `5b2be3f`/others may modify `package.json` — check whether root `package.json` (Tier 1) is modified in this range and by which commits. The doc's claim that only 542ac65 carries a statement needs the full list of Tier-1-touching commits to be meaningful.
13. "Every commit carries `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5`; no human co-author or reviewer trailer appears on any of them." — verify across all 14 commits with `git log --format='%H%n%B' ec9d161..7b9b5dc | grep -i co-authored`. Is the trailer really "Claude Sonnet 5" on ALL 14?
14. "**The server-side gate is intact and holding.** PR #59 is `REVIEW_REQUIRED` / `BLOCKED`. Branch protection on `develop` requires 1 approving review with `require_code_owner_reviews: true`, and CODEOWNERS has requested `tier-1-approvers`, `pwa-squad-a`, `pwa-squad-b`, `tier-2-approvers`. **You are the PR author, so you cannot self-approve.** Also note `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`."
   - Verify via `gh pr view 59 --json ...` (mergeStateStatus, reviewDecision, author, reviewRequests) and `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches/develop/protection` (read-only GET).
   - CRITICAL: verify the PR AUTHOR. The document addresses the reader as "you" and says "You are the PR author". All 14 commits are by TimLavelle. Report who the actual PR author is. The document's reader is marcel.a.n.navarro (GitHub login unknown — find it with `gh api user --jq .login`).
   - Verify the requested reviewer teams list exactly.
   - Verify `dismiss_stale_reviews`.
15. "the last review on PR #59 predates all 14 commits and now reads `DISMISSED`." — verify via `gh pr view 59 --json reviews` / `gh api repos/.../pulls/59/reviews`. Report the real state and timestamps vs commit timestamps.
16. Doc header says "**PR #59**" for branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` — verify PR #59 is really that branch's PR and its target branch.

Report terse findings organised as WRONG / STALE / OVERSTATED / UNVERIFIABLE / CORRECT with exact real values.

     2	
     3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
     4	
     5	**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
     6	covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
     7	decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
     8	renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
     9	Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
    10	**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
    11	elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
    12	right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
    13	component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
    14	component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
    15	and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
    16	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
    17	resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
    18	render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
    19	(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
    20	below for single-parent internal components still applies there.
